stemMd:
**Text 1**
A simplified transit map omits geographic detail so passengers can quickly identify connections. Its distortion of distance is acceptable because route choice is its main purpose.

**Text 2**
Transit maps are also used to judge whether walking between stations is practical. A diagram that greatly exaggerates a short gap can discourage a useful walk, even when it clearly shows train connections.

The authors would most likely agree that

options.label: B
options.textMd: a map must contain every street to be useful.

options.label: C
options.textMd: all geographic distortion makes a map useless.

options.label: D
options.textMd: the usefulness of a map depends partly on the task a reader uses it to perform.

explanationMd: Text 1 evaluates the diagram by route connections; Text 2 adds walking decisions. Both link usefulness to a user task, although they emphasize different tasks and therefore assess distortion differently.
